content.title: LeBron James records first father-son assist to Bronny James Jr. in Lakers win over Nets
content.text: There are moments in sports that feel scripted. And then there are moments that feel impossible.Both occurred Friday night at Crypto.com Arena.Midway through the second quarter of a 116–99 win over the Nets, LeBron James received a pass from his son Bronny and was immediately double-teamed. So he did something he’s done throughout his 23-year NBA career.Los Angeles Lakers forward LeBron James dribbles against Brooklyn Nets forward Ziaire Williams during the first half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images William Liang-Imagn ImagesHe made the right basketball play.AdvertisementJames found the open man on the left wing, who just so happened to be his son. The younger James faked the pass to the corner and then shot a wide-open three-pointer.Swish.History.For the first time in the history of the NBA, a father assisted his son.Forget all the controversy, all the talk, all the chatter and let that sit for a second.Regardless of what you think about James or his son, this was more than just an assist in the box score. More than just a spectacle on NBA Opening Night. This was legacy in Lakers’ purple and gold. Bloodlines turned into basketball poetry.“Well, I mean, just not taking it for granted and just being in the moment of us being on the floor once again,” James said afterward, his voice carrying the weight of someone who has seen everything — and still somehow found something new on Friday. “That’s two games back-to-back… definitely a cool moment for us and also for our family.”Bronny James of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a three point basket during the game against the Brooklyn Nets on March 27, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) NBAE via Getty ImagesCool.AdvertisementThat’s certainly one way to describe it, but how do you properly explain what it means to share the same hardwood with your son— not in a driveway, not in a gym tucked away from the world, but under the lights, in front of thousands, with millions watching across the country and delivering a pass that he drains a three on? How do you quantify something that feels more surreal than a meaningful moment?It’s easy to forget because the NBA machine doesn’t slow down for sentiment.Less than three years ago, Bronny James collapsed during a workout at USC, his future hanging in the balance after a cardiac arrest that forced everyone to confront something far bigger than basketball.A congenital heart defect. A long road back. Quiet doubt lingering in the background.AdvertisementAnd now?“I’m more comfortable shooting behind the NBA line, and I’m more comfortable shooting without thinking,” Bronny said, the words simple but loaded, like a man rediscovering not just his rhythm, but himself.“I’ve been wanting to play basketball my whole life… It’s a dream come true. I love every single second of it.”LeBron James of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the game against the Brooklyn Nets on March 27, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) NBAE via Getty ImagesYou could feel that Friday night. Not just in the shot, but in the space between moments. In the way James glanced at his son after he made the shot. In the way the arena came to life. Like everyone understood they had just witnessed something that may not come around twice.James Jr. has been getting more playing time in the last two games because of the injury to Lakers starting guard Marcus Smart. He’s spent most of this season bouncing between the Lakers and the G League, where he’s been working on his outside shot.AdvertisementOn Friday, he felt like he proved that he belongs beyond the last name stitched across the back of his jersey.His confidence growing, he shared that after the game that the last time he played his dad 1-on-1 he was eight years old in the backyard in Miami when LeBron was playing with the Heat. After defeating his dad, the older James broke the backboard so they couldn’t play again.“I don’t know if this story came out, but the last time I played him one on one he broke a backboard at our house in Miami,” said James Jr. smiling.Bronny James of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the game against the Brooklyn Nets on March 27, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) NBAE via Getty ImagesJames glared at his son from across the locker room, but deep down you know he was beaming with pride.AdvertisementJames has spent 21 seasons building a legacy brick by brick, assist by assist, championship by championship. He has chased ghosts and rewritten expectations and turned longevity into an art form. And yet, in one simple pass, he may have authored the most human moment of his entire career.Not another dunk. Not another title. Not another record.Just a simple pass.“We’ve done that thousands of times,” Bronny said, smiling through the familiarity of it all. “It was a special moment with us two and there’s a lot more to come down the road.”LeBron James of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket during the game against the Brooklyn Nets on March 27, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) NBAE via Getty ImagesMaybe there is.Maybe there isn’t.That’s the thing about moments like this — they don’t promise anything beyond themselves. They just exist, glowing briefly, before becoming memory.AdvertisementBut for one night in Los Angeles, under the bright lights of the arena, a player didn’t just pass the ball to his teammate, but a father passed something far greater on to his son that they will remember for the rest of their lives.Download The California Post App, follow us on social, and subscribe to our newsletters California Post News: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedInCalifornia Post Sports Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, XCalifornia Post Opinion California Post Newsletters: Sign up here!California Post App: Download here!Home delivery: Sign up here!Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!
